back: [[kw:Q1]] (first quartile): about 25% of data below it.
[[kw:Q2]] (second quartile): the [[imp:median]]; 50% below.
[[kw:Q3]] (third quartile): about 75% below.
They divide an ordered data set into four equal parts.
Ordered (n=15). Q2 (median) = 18 (8th value).
The range of the middle 50% of the data.
$$\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1$$
Resistant to outliers; used to build boxplots and detect outliers.

cards.front: Compute the IQR for nuclear plant data: Q1=10, Q3=31
back: The middle 50% of countries have between 10 and 31 nuclear plants.
Compute fences:
Lower fence = $Q_1 - 1.5 \times \text{IQR}$
Upper fence = $Q_3 + 1.5 \times \text{IQR}$
Any data value outside the fences is an [[imp:outlier]].
cards.front: How do you use IQR to identify [[kw:outliers]]?

104 > 62.5 → [[imp:outlier]].

back: Minimum, $Q_1$, Median ($Q_2$), $Q_3$, Maximum.
Used to construct a box-and-whisker plot.

cards.front: How do you draw a [[kw:box-and-whisker plot]]?
back: 1. Draw horizontal scale.
2. Plot the five-number summary above it.
3. Draw a box from $Q_1$ to $Q_3$ with a vertical line at the median.
4. Draw whiskers from the box to min and max.
The box shows the [[imp:middle 50%]] of data.
The distribution is [[imp:skewed right]] (positively skewed).
The tail on the right side is longer than the left.

back: Percentiles divide data into 100 equal parts. $P_k$: $k$% of data fall below it.

cards.front: Define [[kw:percentiles]] and their relationship to quartiles.
What does it mean to be at the 60th percentile?
back: You scored higher than 60% of the group.
It is a measure of relative standing, not absolute performance.
Fractiles that divide data into 10 equal parts.
Used similarly to percentiles but coarser.
The number of standard deviations a value $x$ is from the mean.
$$z = \frac{x - \mu}{\sigma}$$
Positive: above mean; Negative: below mean; Zero: at mean.

cards.front: Vehicle speeds: μ=56 mph, σ=4 mph. Find z for 62 mph and 47 mph.
back: 47 mph: $z = (47-56)/4 = -2.25$ (unusually slow).
Unusual if $z < -2$ or $z > 2$ (bell‑shaped).
